back:
• Potent antiemetic effect
• Reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV)
• Often combined with 5-HT3 antagonists
• Enhances quality of life during active treatment

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: In the management of end-stage malignancies, corticosteroids like [___] are frequently utilized for their palliative effect in stimulating appetite and improving the sense of well-being.
back:
Prednisone.
• Acts as an appetite stimulant to combat anorexia.
• Promotes weight gain and improves energy levels.
• Enhances the patient's general sense of well-being.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A 60-year-old male with metastatic lung cancer presents with severe headaches and projectile vomiting. Which corticosteroid is the drug of choice for the palliative reduction of peritumoral brain edema?
back:
Dexamethasone.
• Potent anti-inflammatory effect.
• Reduces intracranial pressure caused by cerebral edema.
• Minimizes neurological symptoms in palliative care.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Explain the palliative role of bisphosphonates in patients with metastatic bone disease receiving long-term corticosteroid therapy.
back:
• Inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.
• Reduce the risk of pathological fractures.
• Provide relief from chronic bone pain.
• Counteract steroid-induced osteoporosis.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Contrast the primary clinical objectives of 'Curative' chemotherapy with those of 'Palliative' chemotherapy in advanced malignancies.
back:
• Curative: Eradication of every neoplastic cell for long-term survival.
• Palliative: Alleviation of symptoms and avoidance of life-threatening toxicity.
• Intent: Focuses on quality of life over extending survival.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
coreConcept: Palliative Hormonal Therapy in Breast Cancer
front: Identify the Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM) used for the palliative treatment of advanced estrogen-receptor (ER) positive breast cancer.
back:
Tamoxifen.
• Competes with natural estrogen for receptor binding.
• Suppresses growth-promoting effects in breast tissue.
• Standard first-line therapy for metastatic ER+ disease.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
coreConcept: LHRH Analogs in Palliative Prostate Care
front: In metastatic prostate cancer, synthetic LHRH/GnRH analogs like [___] are used to provide palliative relief from bone pain by reducing testosterone synthesis.
back:
Leuprolide (or Goserelin).
• Occupies GnRH receptors in the pituitary.
• Leads to desensitization and inhibited LH/FSH release.
• Results in 'chemical castration' for symptom relief.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A patient with advanced solid tumors is receiving emetogenic cisplatin. Which corticosteroid is added to the regimen specifically for the palliative prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting?
back:
Dexamethasone.
• Used in high doses to reduce emetic effects.
• Effective adjunct for both chemotherapy and general anesthesia-induced nausea.
• Improves tolerance of palliative regimens.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Describe the mechanism by which antiandrogens, such as Flutamide, provide palliative benefit in metastatic prostate cancer.
back:
• Competitively bind to androgen receptors.
• Prevent the translocation of the androgen-receptor complex into the nucleus.
• Block the growth-promoting effects of testosterone on prostatic tissue.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Distinguish between 'Adjuvant' chemotherapy and 'Palliative' chemotherapy regarding their clinical timing and intent.
back:
• Adjuvant: Supplemental treatment after surgery/radiation to destroy micrometastases.
• Palliative: Treatment for disseminated/advanced disease to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Define the concept of a 'Hormone Responsive' tumor as it relates to palliative hormonal manipulation.
back:
• A tumor that regresses upon treatment with a specific hormone.
• Distinguished from hormone-dependent (regress upon removal of a stimulus).
• Key concept in selecting palliative hormonal agents.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: In the context of palliative oncology, the glucocorticoid [___] is commonly prescribed to stimulate appetite and promote weight gain in patients with advanced malignancies.
back: * Drug: Prednisone. * Purpose: Enhances appetite and sense of well-being. * Clinical context: Used to manage cancer-associated anorexia-cachexia syndrome.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A 65-year-old male with metastatic prostate cancer presents with a sudden exacerbation of bone pain and urinary symptoms shortly after starting Leuprolide. Identify the pharmacological cause of this 'tumor flare'.
back: * Cause: Initial GnRH agonist-induced surge in LH and FSH. * Result: Transient increase in testosterone levels before pituitary desensitization. * Management: Often co-administered with flutamide to block receptors.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Explain the role of Dexamethasone in the palliative management of patients with primary or metastatic brain tumors.
back: * Indication: Management of peritumoral edema. * Mechanism: Reduces capillary permeability and intracranial pressure. * Symptom Relief: Alleviates headaches and focal neurological deficits.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Contrast the primary therapeutic objective of palliative chemotherapy with that of adjuvant chemotherapy.
back: * Palliative: Alleviation of symptoms and improving quality of life in advanced disease. * Adjuvant: Eradication of micrometastases following primary surgery to prevent recurrence.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Identify the drug used to reduce the risk of skeletal-related events, such as pathological fractures and bone pain, in patients with advanced bone metastases.
back: * Drug: Bisphosphonates (e.g., Zoledronic acid). * Mechanism: Inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. * Palliative Role: Significant reduction in bone pain and hypercalcemia of malignancy.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: In the palliative treatment of postmenopausal women with estrogen receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer, [___] inhibitors are used to block the peripheral synthesis of estrogen.
back: * Drug Class: Aromatase inhibitors (e.g., Anastrozole, Letrozole). * Mechanism: Inhibits the conversion of androstenedione to estrone in peripheral tissues. * Population: Primarily indicated for postmenopausal patients.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A patient with advanced pancreatic cancer is started on Gemcitabine. Define the 'clinical benefit' this drug aims to provide in this palliative setting.
back: * Definition: Improvement in pain, performance status, and weight gain. * Note: Focuses on symptomatic relief even if objective tumor shrinkage is limited.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Explain how Dexamethasone is utilized to improve the safety profile of highly emetogenic palliative chemotherapy regimens.
back: * Role: Adjunctive antiemetic. * Synergy: Potentiates the effects of 5-HT3 receptor antagonists (e.g., Ondansetron). * Benefit: Reduces the incidence and severity of nausea and vomiting.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Distinguish between hormone-responsive and hormone-dependent tumors in the management of advanced hormone-sensitive cancers.
back: * Hormone-responsive: Tumor regresses upon administration of a specific hormone. * Hormone-dependent: Tumor regresses upon the removal of a specific hormonal stimulus (e.g., estrogen or testosterone).

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: In the management of advanced prostate cancer, the antiandrogen [___] is used to competitively inhibit the binding of testosterone to its target receptor.
back: * Drug: Flutamide (or Bicalutamide). * Mechanism: Competitive androgen receptor antagonist. * Use: Often paired with GnRH analogs to achieve total androgen blockade.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: In the rehabilitation of a patient with primary adrenocortical insufficiency (Addison disease), the drug [___] is typically administered in divided doses to mimic the natural diurnal cortisol rhythm.
back:
• Hydrocortisone
• Identical to natural cortisol
• Dosage: 2/3 in morning, 1/3 in afternoon
• Prevents life-threatening adrenal crisis

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A patient in physical rehabilitation for rheumatoid arthritis has been on long-term Prednisone. They now present with a vertebral compression fracture. Identify the primary metabolic pathophysiology.
back:
• Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis
• Suppression of intestinal Calcium absorption
• Inhibition of bone formation
• Decreased sex hormone synthesis

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which glucocorticoids exert their anti-inflammatory action during the management of inflammatory disorders.
back:
• Inhibition of Phospholipase A2 (blocks arachidonic acid release)
• Decreased production of prostaglandins and leukotrienes
• Stabilization of mast cell and basophil membranes
• Reduced release of proinflammatory cytokines

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Contrast the primary dose-limiting toxicities of the microtubule inhibitors Vincristine and Vinblastine encountered during oncology rehabilitation.
back:
• Vincristine: Neurotoxicity (paresthesias, foot drop, ataxia); minimal myelosuppression
• Vinblastine: Potent myelosuppression; less neurotoxic
• Both block mitosis in M-phase by binding tubulin

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Specify the role of the Dexamethasone suppression test in the diagnostic workup of a patient with suspected Cushing syndrome.
back:
• Synthetic glucocorticoid used to distinguish hypercortisolism
• Normal individuals: Cortisol release is suppressed
• Cushing syndrome: Cortisol release is NOT suppressed
• Distinguishes true Cushing from anxiety/depression (pseudo-Cushing)

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A patient undergoing cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure is prescribed [___], a mineralocorticoid antagonist that avoids the side effect of gynecomastia.
back:
• Eplerenone
• Specifically binds mineralocorticoid receptors
• Lacks the anti-androgen effects of Spironolactone
• Approved for hypertension and reduced ejection fraction heart failure

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A patient receiving ifosfamide chemotherapy develops gross hematuria during a rehabilitation session. Identify the causative metabolite and the mandatory preventative agent.
back:
• Metabolite: Acrolein (toxic to bladder mucosa)
• Preventative Agent: Mesna (sodium 2-mercaptoethane sulfonate)
• Mesna neutralizes acrolein in the bladder
• Aggressive hydration is also required

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Discuss the pathophysiology of synergistic cardiotoxicity in a patient receiving both Trastuzumab and Doxorubicin during rehabilitative monitoring.
back:
• Doxorubicin: Generates iron-dependent oxygen free radicals causing myocyte damage
• Trastuzumab: Blocks HER2 signaling essential for myocyte repair
• Result: Dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy/congestive heart failure
• Monitored via LVEF (ECHO or MUGA)

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: In the rehabilitation of a colorectal cancer patient on Irinotecan, distinguish between the management of early-onset and late-onset diarrhea.
back:
• Early (within 24h): Cholinergic event; treated with Atropine
• Late (2-10 days): Potentially life-threatening; treated with high-dose Loperamide
• Mechanism: Topoisomerase I inhibition

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Identify the high-yield therapeutic indication for Betamethasone when administered intramuscularly to a mother in preterm labor.
back:
• Acceleration of fetal lung maturation
• Stimulates production of pulmonary surfactant
• Reduces risk of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
• Administered 48 hours preceding premature delivery

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: The synthetic mineralocorticoid often used to supplement patients with Addison disease who have persistent hyponatremia and dehydration despite hydrocortisone therapy is [___].
back:
* Fludrocortisone
* Provides potent salt-retaining activity
* Corrects electrolyte imbalances by mimicking aldosterone effects in the distal tubule.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A patient on long-term prednisone for rheumatoid arthritis presents with a 'moon face,' buffalo hump, and purple striae. Identify the metabolic process leading to the muscle wasting seen in this condition.
back:
* Protein catabolism
* Glucocorticoids increase the breakdown of muscle protein
* This provides amino acids for hepatic gluconeogenesis to raise plasma glucose levels.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Explain how glucocorticoids inhibit the production of prostaglandins and leukotrienes at the start of the inflammatory cascade.
back:
* Inhibit phospholipase A2
* This prevents the release of arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids
* Directly blocks the precursor shared by both the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase pathways.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: In a patient requiring long-term steroid therapy, contrast the physiological rationale for using alternate-day administration versus a split-dose (2/3 AM, 1/3 PM) regimen.
back:
* Alternate-day: Prevents HPA axis suppression by allowing the axis to function on 'off' days
* Split-dose: Mimics natural diurnal cortisol rhythm
* Only alternate-day dosing allows HPA recovery.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Describe the specific hepatic conversion required for Prednisone to exert its pharmacological effects in the body.
back:
* Conversion to Prednisolone
* Mediated by hepatic 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
* Prednisone acts as an inactive prodrug until this enzymatic step occurs.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Cushing syndrome is distinguished from normal physiological states using the [___] suppression test.
back:
* Dexamethasone suppression test
* Normal individuals show decreased cortisol levels due to feedback inhibition
* Cushing syndrome patients fail to suppress cortisol secretion.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks gestation is at risk for premature delivery. Which specific corticosteroid is administered to accelerate fetal lung maturation, and why?
back:
* Betamethasone (or Dexamethasone)
* High glucocorticoid activity promotes surfactant production
* These agents have low maternal protein binding and cross the placenta easily.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: How does the co-administration of Ketoconazole affect a patient with Cushing syndrome differently than the use of Spironolactone?
back:
* Ketoconazole: Inhibits all gonadal and adrenal steroid hormone synthesis enzymes
* Spironolactone: Competes for the mineralocorticoid receptor and antagonizes androgens
* Ketoconazole inhibits biosynthesis; Spironolactone blocks receptors.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Contrast the effects of glucocorticoids on circulating leukocyte counts, specifically comparing neutrophils to lymphocytes.
back:
* Neutrophils: Count increases (due to decreased margination/vascular exit)
* Lymphocytes: Count decreases (redistribution to lymphoid tissues)
* Also leads to decreased monocytes and eosinophils.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Identify the primary enzyme located in the kidney that protects mineralocorticoid receptors from being overwhelmed by high levels of circulating cortisol.
back:
* 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2
* Converts active cortisol into inactive cortisone
* Ensures renal mineralocorticoid receptors respond specifically to aldosterone.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: The corticosteroid [___] is specifically indicated for the palliative reduction of peritumoral edema and intracranial pressure in patients with brain metastases.
back:
• Dexamethasone
• Reduces cerebral swelling
• Improves focal neurological deficits via anti-inflammatory action

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A 68-year-old patient with inoperable, metastatic gastric carcinoma is started on chemotherapy. Describe the primary objective of this intervention if it is classified as 'Palliative.'
back:
• Alleviation of symptoms (e.g., pain, dyspnea)
• Enhancement of quality of life
• Slowing of disease progression without the expectation of a total cure

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Explain the mechanism and clinical rationale for using glucocorticoids like Prednisone palliatively in advanced cancer patients beyond their cytotoxic effects.
back:
• Appetite stimulation to combat cancer cachexia
• Induction of euphoria/well-being
• Management of tumor-related inflammatory pain

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Contrast the palliative mechanisms of Bisphosphonates versus Corticosteroids in the management of metastatic bone pain.
back:
• Bisphosphonates: Inhibit osteoclast activity to reduce bone resorption and turnover.
• Corticosteroids: Reduce inflammation and edema-mediated nerve compression at the tumor site.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Palliative hormonal management for advanced, symptomatic prostate cancer primarily utilizes [___] to achieve chemical castration and reduce metastatic bone pain.
back:
• LHRH Agonists (e.g., Leuprolide or Goserelin)
• Inhibits testosterone production by the testes
• Provides symptomatic relief from androgen-dependent bone metastases

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: In palliative oncological management, the long-acting glucocorticoid [___] is the agent of choice for reducing intracranial pressure caused by peritumoral edema in patients with brain metastases.
back:
• Dexamethasone
• It minimizes cerebral edema through potent anti-inflammatory effects.
• It is preferred over other steroids due to its minimal mineralocorticoid activity and high potency.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A 70-year-old male with hormone-refractory metastatic prostate cancer experiences debilitating skeletal pain. The specific palliative regimen indicated for symptom control in this patient involves combining Prednisone with [___].
back:
• Mitoxantrone
• It is an anthracenedione that intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II.
• In this setting, the goal is specifically palliating bone pain rather than achieving long-term survival or cure.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Explain the biological rationale for utilizing glucocorticoids like Prednisone in the palliative care of advanced cancer patients suffering from cachexia and lethargy.
back:
• Glucocorticoids act as appetite stimulants and promote a sense of well-being (euphoria).
• They provide energy to combat stress-induced exhaustion.
• This palliative use focuses on improving quality of life and nutritional intake.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A patient with colon cancer receives chemotherapy after a successful resection (Adjuvant), while another with lung metastases receives drugs to reduce symptoms (Palliative). Contrast these scenarios based on their primary therapeutic intent.
back:
• Adjuvant: Administered post-surgery to eliminate occult micrometastases and prevent recurrence.
• Palliative: Administered in advanced/disseminated disease to alleviate symptoms and extend survival.
• Palliative care treats cancer as a chronic, non-curable condition.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Identify the major therapeutic objective of palliative drug therapy in advanced neoplastic disease when total tumor eradication is no longer clinically feasible.
back:
• Alleviation of symptoms (e.g., pain, nausea, dyspnea).
• Avoidance of life-threatening toxicity.
• Maintenance of a 'near-normal' existence and optimal quality of life for the patient.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: The specific chemotherapeutic approach aimed at alleviating symptoms and extending survival in advanced cancers without the expectation of eradicating every neoplastic cell is termed [___] chemotherapy.
back:
• Palliative Chemotherapy
• Focuses on symptom regression.
• Often involves lower-intensity doses to balance quality of life with tumor control.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: A chemotherapy patient presents with persistent vomiting refractory to standard anti-emetics. Addition of [___] to the regimen is indicated specifically to reduce emetic effects and improve palliative outcomes.
back:
• Dexamethasone
• It reduces the production of proinflammatory cytokines and inhibits phospholipase A2.
• This helps prevent both acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Discuss the mechanism by which glucocorticoids provide palliative relief in malignant spinal cord compression compared to their anti-inflammatory role in chronic disease.
back:
• In malignancy, they stabilize mast cell membranes and decrease capillary permeability.
• This reduces local inflammation and edema at the compression site.
• This immediate effect prevents irreversible neurological damage and palliates severe pain.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Contrast the metabolic benefit of using glucocorticoids for appetite stimulation with the physiological risk of drug-induced diabetes during palliative care.
back:
• Benefit: Stimulates lipolysis and protein catabolism to provide energy building blocks.
• Risk: Glucocorticoids favor gluconeogenesis and inhibit peripheral glucose uptake.
• Result: While improving appetite, they may induce hyperglycemia and iatrogenic Cushing-like syndrome.

category: Describe the drugs used for palliative therapy in various tumours
front: Specify the cytotoxic drug used in palliative protocols for prostate cancer that is primarily associated with reducing bone pain rather than Increasing growth-free survival.
back:
• Mitoxantrone
• It is used when the tumor is hormone-refractory.
• It is an antitumor antibiotic (anthracenedione) that causes DNA strand scission via free radical production.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To prevent the complication of hemorrhagic cystitis during high-dose ifosfamide therapy, the sulfhydryl compound [___] is administered to neutralize acrolein in the bladder.
back:
Mesna (sodium 2-mercaptoethane sulfonate).
• Binds and inactivates the toxic metabolite acrolein.
• Essential during high-dose cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide.
• Requires concurrent aggressive hydration.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A 28-year-old woman in preterm labor at 30 weeks gestation is administered intramuscular betamethasone. Describe the specific clinical goal for the neonate regarding this pharmacological intervention.
back:
Accelerated fetal lung maturation.
• Stimulates production of pulmonary surfactant.
• Prevents neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS).
• Most effective when given 48 hours before delivery.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Ketoconazole reduces cortisol levels in patients with inoperable Cushing syndrome.
back:
Nonselective inhibition of steroidogenesis.
• Inhibits cytochrome P450 enzymes (cholesterol side-chain cleavage).
• Blocks 17α-hydroxylase and 11β-hydroxylase.
• Reduces all adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the clinical side-effect profiles of Spironolactone and Eplerenone when used as aldosterone antagonists in hyperaldosteronism.
back:
Spironolactone: Causes gynecomastia and menstrual irregularities (anti-androgenic activity).
• Eplerenone: Highly selective for mineralocorticoid receptors; avoids androgen receptor-related side effects.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify the specific cytoprotective agent used to minimize the risk of dose-dependent cardiomyopathy in patients receiving high cumulative doses of Doxorubicin.
back:
Dexrazoxane.
• Acts as an intracellular iron chelator.
• Prevents iron-dependent superoxide radical formation.
• Protects the myocardium from anthracycline-induced oxidative damage.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: In cancer chemotherapy, Prednisone is frequently utilized for its lymphocytolytic effects and its ability to manage the common complication of [___] to improve patient quality of life.
back:
Anorexia (or weight loss).
• Acts as an appetite stimulant.
• Produces euphoria and a sense of well-being.
• Reduces chemotherapy-induced systemic inflammation.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient with a metastatic brain tumor develops severe headaches and altered consciousness due to peritumor edema. Identify the glucocorticoid drug and its primary role in reducing this specific complication.
back:
Dexamethasone.
• Reduces increased intracranial pressure.
• Specifically targets and minimizes cerebral edema.
• Often used post-brain surgery or during cranial irradiation.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Describe the specific dietary restrictions and biochemical rationale required for patients treated with the alkylating agent Procarbazine.
back:
Avoid Tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, wine).
• Procarbazine is a weak MAO inhibitor.
• Prevents hypertensive crisis.
• Also produces a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Differentiate the therapeutic roles of Folinic acid (Leucovorin) and Filgrastim (G-CSF) in managing chemotherapy-related complications.
back:
Folinic acid: Specifically 'rescues' cells from Methotrexate toxicity by bypassing DHFR inhibition.
• Filgrastim: Stimulates granulocyte production to shorten/prevent neutropenia from general myelosuppression.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify the pharmacological agent administered to counteract the acute cholinergic crisis, including salivation and early diarrhea, occurring during Irinotecan infusion.
back:
Atropine.
• Anticholinergic agent used for 'early' diarrhea (<24 hours).
• Blocks muscarinic receptors triggered by irinotecan.
• Note: Delayed diarrhea (>24 hours) requires Loperamide.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To prevent hemorrhagic cystitis during high-dose cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide therapy, the sulfhydryl compound [___] is administered to neutralize toxic acrolein in the bladder.
back:
• Drug: Mesna.
• Function: Acts as a regional detoxifier by binding to acrolein in the urine.
• Administration: Usually paired with aggressive intravenous hydration to maintain high urine output.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A 55-year-old male with a high-grade glioma develops signs of increased intracranial pressure and severe headache. Identify the specific corticosteroid preferred for managing this complication of brain malignancy.
back:
• Drug: Dexamethasone.
• Rationale: Possesses high glucocorticoid potency with minimal mineralocorticoid (salt-retaining) activity.
• Clinical Goal: Reduces peritumoral edema and intracranial pressure without worsening peripheral edema.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the pharmacological role of Allopurinol when administered prior to chemotherapy for highly proliferative hematologic malignancies like Burkitt’s Lymphoma.
back:
• Objective: Prevention of Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
• Mechanism: Inhibits xanthine oxidase.
• Result: Prevents hyperuricemia by blocking the conversion of purine metabolites into uric acid, protecting renal function.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the therapeutic purpose of Leucovorin (Folinic Acid) when co-administered with Methotrexate versus its role when combined with 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU).
back:
• With Methotrexate: 'Rescue' therapy to provide reduced folates to normal cells, bypassing inhibited dihydrofolate reductase.
• With 5-FU: Potentiation agent that stabilizes the ternary complex with thymidylate synthase, increasing drug efficacy.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: State the clinical indication and primary mechanism of Dexrazoxane in the management of complications arising from chronic Doxorubicin therapy.
back:
• Indication: Prevention of anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity and cardiomyopathy.
• Mechanism: Intracellular iron-chelating agent.
• Action: Reduces the formation of iron-anthracycline complexes that generate damaging oxygen free radicals in myocardial tissue.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: In the management of metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer, the drug [___] is administered orally alongside Prednisone to inhibit the CYP17 enzyme and reduce extra-testicular testosterone production.
back: • Abiraterone acetate • Inhibits 17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase • Prevents androgen synthesis in adrenal glands and tumor tissue • Co-administered with Prednisone to suppress secondary mineralocorticoid excess.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A 5-year-old child being treated for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia with a high-dose Prednisone-containing regimen develops sudden-onset, severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Identify the likely pharmacological complication.
back: • Acute pancreatitis • Rare but serious adverse effect of high-dose glucocorticoids • Requires immediate drug cessation • Diagnosed via elevated serum amylase and lipase levels.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the therapeutic rationale for administering high-dose Dexamethasone immediately following the surgical resection of an intracranial tumor.
back: • Reduces peritumoral cerebral edema • Minimizes intracranial pressure • Potent anti-inflammatory action with negligible mineralocorticoid effect • Palliative relief of neurological symptoms post-operatively.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the pathophysiological mechanisms of "early-onset" versus "late-onset" diarrhea associated with Irinotecan therapy.
back: • Early-onset: Cholinergic surge (inhibits acetylcholinesterase); treat with Atropine • Late-onset: Secretory toxicity from SN-38 metabolite; treat with high-dose Loperamide • Late form can be life-threatening.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Specify the clinical role of Glucocorticoids in the palliative management of subacute thyroiditis or malignant exophthalmos.
back: • Reduces orbital inflammation and pressure • Suppresses immune-mediated thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin effects • Provides relief from heat, swelling, and tenderness • Reduces pro-inflammatory cytokine release.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Patients with an inherited deficiency of the enzyme [___] are at extreme risk for life-threatening neurotoxicity and pancytopenia when treated with standard doses of 5-Fluorouracil.
back: • Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) • Primary catabolic enzyme for 5-FU metabolism • Deficiency results in toxic drug accumulation • Affects approximately 5% of the population.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient starting Pemetrexed for non-small cell lung cancer is prescribed daily folic acid and vitamin B12. Identify the clinical goal of this pharmacological strategy.
back: • Minimizes hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicities • Reduces severity of myelosuppression • Does not compromise antitumor efficacy • Often paired with dexamethasone to prevent skin rashes.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Detail the pharmacological mechanism by which Dexrazoxane provides cytoprotection to the myocardium during high-dose anthracycline therapy.
back: • Intracellular iron-chelating agent • Inhibits formation of anthracycline-iron complexes • Reduces production of superoxide and hydroxyl free radicals • Minimizes oxidative damage to cardiac membranes.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Distinguish between 5-Fluorouracil and its oral derivative Capecitabine regarding their activation sites.
back: • 5-FU: Intravenous; activated systemically via multiple enzymatic steps • Capecitabine: Oral prodrug; converted to 5-FU specifically within tumor tissue by thymidine phosphorylase • Capecitabine offers improved tumor-site selectivity.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify two clinical benefits of using Prednisone in cancer chemotherapy protocols beyond its direct lymphocytolytic effects on malignant cells.
back: • Stimulates appetite to combat cancer cachexia • Anti-emetic properties (reduces chemotherapy-induced vomiting) • Reduces peritumoral inflammation • Manages transfusion or drug-induced allergic reactions.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To prevent hemorrhagic cystitis caused by the metabolite acrolein during high-dose cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide therapy, the sulfhydryl compound [___] is administered.
back:
Mesna (sodium 2-mercaptoethane sulfonate).
• Binds and neutralizes acrolein in the urinary bladder.
• Requires concurrent aggressive intravenous hydration.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A 10-year-old with ALL develops acute renal failure and severe hyperuricemia post-chemotherapy. The pharmacological agent used to enzymatically convert uric acid into the more soluble allantoin is [___].
back:
Rasburicase.
• Recombinant urate oxidase enzyme.
• Prevents urate nephropathy in Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
• More rapid acting than allopurinol.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the role of Leucovorin (Folinic acid) in bypassing the metabolic blockade induced by high-dose Methotrexate therapy.
back:
• Methotrexate inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Leucovorin provides a direct source of reduced folates (N5-formyl-FH4).
• It bypasses the inhibited DHFR to replenish the tetrahydrofolate pool for DNA synthesis.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the two primary clinical indications for the adjunct agent Dexrazoxane in a patient receiving Doxorubicin therapy.
back:
• Cardioprotection: Prevents iron-mediated free radical damage (for cumulative doses >300 mg/m²).
• Extravasation: Acts as an antidote for accidental anthracycline leakage to prevent tissue necrosis.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Name the specific receptor targeted by Ondansetron to manage acute chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) occurring within the first 24 hours.
back:
5-HT3 Receptors.
• Located on vagal afferents and in the Chemoreceptor Trigger Zone (CTZ).
• Standard prophylaxis for highly emetogenic regimens.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To shorten the duration of severe neutropenia and reduce the risk of infection after myelosuppressive chemotherapy, the G-CSF analog [___] is administered.
back:
Filgrastim.
• Stimulates proliferation and differentiation of neutrophil progenitors.
• Used to prevent febrile neutropenia.
• Administered 24 hours after chemotherapy completion.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A metastatic breast cancer patient presents with confusion, constipation, and serum calcium of 14 mg/dL. The class of drugs used to inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption in this complication is [___].
back:
Bisphosphonates (e.g., Zoledronic acid).
• Inhibits bone resorption and induces osteoclast apoptosis.
• Manages hypercalcemia of malignancy.
• Prevents skeletal-related events in bone metastases.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the biochemical basis for reducing the dose of 6-Mercaptopurine by 75% when a patient is simultaneously prescribed Allopurinol.
back:
• 6-MP is inactivated by Xanthine Oxidase.
• Allopurinol inhibits Xanthine Oxidase.
• Concurrent use results in decreased 6-MP clearance and severe, potentially fatal bone marrow toxicity.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Distinguish between the primary purpose of prophylactic dexamethasone in Paclitaxel therapy versus its specific utility in Docetaxel therapy.
back:
• Paclitaxel: Prevents severe hypersensitivity reactions to the Cremophor vehicle.
• Docetaxel: Primarily prevents fluid retention (peripheral edema and pleural effusions).

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify the organic thiophosphate cytoprotectant used specifically to reduce the incidence of Cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity.
back:
Amifostine.
• Scavenges free radicals in normal tissues.
• Does not protect tumor cells due to lower alkaline phosphatase activity.
• Also prevents radiation-induced xerostomia.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To mitigate the risk of dose-dependent, irreversible dilated cardiomyopathy associated with Doxorubicin therapy, the iron-chelating agent [___] is utilized.
back:
• Dexrazoxane
• Reduces free radical formation by chelating intracellular iron
• Specifically prevents anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity
• Administered in patients exceeding cumulative dose thresholds

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A 65-year-old male with lung cancer presents with confusion and serum calcium of 13.8 mg/dL. Explain why Zoledronic acid is utilized as the primary pharmacological intervention over hydration alone.
back:
• Directly inhibits osteoclastic bone resorption
• Provides more sustained reduction in serum calcium than diuretics
• Prevents skeletal-related events (fractures) in bone metastases
• Inhibits the enzyme farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the enzymatic mechanism by which Rasburicase prevents nephrotoxicity in patients with high-grade lymphomas undergoing initial induction chemotherapy.
back:
• Recombinant urate oxidase enzyme
• Catalyzes oxidation of uric acid into allantoin
• Allantoin is 10 times more soluble than uric acid
• Prevents renal urate crystal deposition in Tumor Lysis Syndrome

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Distinguish between the therapeutic targets of Octreotide and Phenoxybenzamine when managing medical complications of neuroendocrine tumors.
back:
• Octreotide: Somatostatin receptor agonist used for Carcinoid syndrome/VIPoma to inhibit hormone release
• Phenoxybenzamine: Irreversible α-blocker used for Pheochromocytoma to manage hypertensive crises

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Specify the pharmacological role and protective mechanism of Amifostine in patients receiving high-dose Cisplatin for advanced ovarian carcinoma.
back:
• Cytoprotectant used to reduce Cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity
• Acts as a scavenger for reactive oxygen species (free radicals)
• Hydrolyzed by alkaline phosphatase to an active thiol metabolite
• Selectively protects normal cells over tumor cells

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: The recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) used to reduce the duration of neutropenia following myelosuppressive chemotherapy is [___].
back:
• Filgrastim
• Stimulates proliferation and differentiation of neutrophil precursors
• Activates mature neutrophils to enhance phagocytosis
• Used to prevent febrile neutropenia in high-risk patients

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient receiving the FOLFIRI regimen for colorectal cancer develops profuse, watery diarrhea five days after his infusion. Identify the pharmacological treatment for this 'late-onset' complication.
back:
• High-dose Loperamide
• Manages secretory diarrhea caused by the Irinotecan metabolite SN-38
• Contrasts with 'early' diarrhea, which is cholinergic and treated with Atropine

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the molecular targets of Zoledronic acid and Denosumab in the prevention of skeletal complications from solid tumors.
back:
• Zoledronic acid: Bisphosphonate that inhibits farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase in osteoclasts
• Denosumab: Monoclonal antibody that binds and inhibits RANKL (RANK ligand)
• Both ultimately prevent osteoclast-mediated bone destruction

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Differentiate between the receptor targets of Ondansetron and Aprepitant in the prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV).
back:
• Ondansetron: Selective 5-HT3 (serotonin) receptor antagonist
• Aprepitant: NK1 (substance P) receptor antagonist
• Combination therapy provides superior control for highly emetogenic regimens (e.g., Cisplatin)

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the initial 'tumor flare' phenomenon observed in metastatic prostate cancer patients when beginning Leuprolide therapy.
back:
• Initial stimulation of pituitary GnRH receptors
• Causes a transient surge in LH and FSH release
• Results in a temporary rise in testosterone before receptor downregulation
• Prevented by co-administration of Flutamide (androgen antagonist)

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To prevent hemorrhagic cystitis during Ifosfamide therapy, Mesna is administered to neutralize the toxic metabolite [___] in the bladder.
back: Acrolein. * Mesna provides a sulfhydryl group that binds acrolein. * Prevents urothelial damage. * Requires concurrent aggressive hydration.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient with a high-grade lymphoma develops hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, and acute renal failure within 24 hours of starting chemotherapy. The pathophysiology of this complication involves [___].
back: Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS). * Rapid release of intracellular ions and nucleic acids. * Nucleic acids are metabolized to uric acid, causing crystal nephropathy.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism of the interaction between Allopurinol and 6-Mercaptopurine (6-MP).
back: Inhibition of Xanthine Oxidase. * Allopurinol inhibits Xanthine Oxidase, the primary enzyme for 6-MP catabolism. * Results in toxic levels of 6-MP. * 6-MP dose must be reduced by 75%.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient with metastatic prostate cancer is started on Leuprolide. Contrast the clinical outcome of adding Flutamide versus using Leuprolide monotherapy during the first week.
back: Prevention of 'Tumor Flare'. * Leuprolide (GnRH agonist) causes a transient testosterone surge. * Flutamide (Androgen receptor blocker) prevents symptom worsening (e.g., bone pain, cord compression) during the surge.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify the pharmacological agent used to manage the 'early' acute cholinergic diarrhea associated with Irinotecan infusion.
back: Atropine. * Blocks muscarinic receptors triggered by irinotecan. * Administered during or immediately after infusion. * Distinct from 'late' diarrhea managed with Loperamide.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: According to standard supportive care protocols, Filgrastim (G-CSF) is indicated when the Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) falls below [___] cells/mm³.
back: 500 cells/mm³. * Defines severe neutropenia. * Filgrastim stimulates neutrophil production and maturation. * Reduces the duration of febrile neutropenia.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient with inoperable adrenal cortical carcinoma presents with severe Cushing's Syndrome. Which antifungal agent is used off-label to inhibit all adrenal steroid synthesis?
back: Ketoconazole. * Non-selectively inhibits P450 enzymes (11β-hydroxylase, C17,20-lyase). * Rapidly lowers systemic cortisol levels. * Used as a bridge to further therapy.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which Leucovorin differentiates between its role in Methotrexate therapy versus its role in 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) therapy.
back: * MTX: Acts as 'rescue' by bypassing inhibited DHFR to provide reduced folates. * 5-FU: Acts as 'enhancer' by stabilizing the ternary complex with Thymidylate Synthase. * Increases 5-FU toxicity/efficacy.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the preferred hormonal maintenance therapy for estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer in premenopausal versus postmenopausal women.
back: Premenopausal: Tamoxifen (SERM) is the standard. * Postmenopausal: Aromatase Inhibitors (e.g., Letrozole) are superior. * AIs are ineffective in premenopausal women due to intact ovarian estrogen production.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: State the clinical biochemical indication for the administration of Dexrazoxane in oncology.
back: Prevention of Doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity. * Acts as an iron-chelating agent. * Reduces the formation of iron-anthracycline complexes and subsequent free radical damage to myocytes.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: To mitigate the most prevalent side effect of long-term corticosteroid therapy during physical rehabilitation, patients are often co-prescribed [___] to inhibit bone resorption.
back: * Bisphosphonates (e.g., Alendronate) * Inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone breakdown * Combined with Calcium and Vitamin D

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A patient undergoing cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure following chemotherapy is found to have had excessive free radical damage to his myocardium. Which iron-chelating cytoprotectant could have been used to prevent this specific doxorubicin-induced injury?
back: * Dexrazoxane * Prevents iron-dependent free radical formation * Specifically reduces anthracycline cardiotoxicity

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Describe the physiological pathway by which Bleomycin causes pulmonary fibrosis, necessitating long-term respiratory rehabilitation.
back: * DNA-bleomycin-Fe(II) complex oxidation * Generation of superoxide and hydroxyl radicals * Leads to pneumonitis and irreversible collagen deposition (fibrosis)

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Contrast the primary neurological deficits encountered in patients requiring rehabilitation after treatment with Vincristine versus Cisplatin.
back: * Vincristine: Primarily motor (foot drop, loss of deep tendon reflexes, paralytic ileus). * Cisplatin: Primarily sensory (distal paresthesias) and ototoxicity. * Vincristine affects axons; Cisplatin affects DNA repair.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Identify the sulfur-containing compound used to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis in patients requiring urological rehabilitation after high-dose Ifosfamide therapy.
back: * Mesna (Sodium 2-mercaptoethane sulfonate) * Binds to and neutralizes acrolein in the urine * Prevents bladder wall irritation and fibrosis

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: In a rehabilitation program for a patient with a localized osteoarthritis flare, [___] administration of corticosteroids is preferred to achieve rapid symptomatic relief without systemic HPA axis suppression.
back: * Intra-articular (injection) * Provides localized anti-inflammatory effects * Used for disease flares in noninflammatory joints

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: A 9-year-old on long-term steroids for chronic inflammatory disease presents with a significant decrease in linear growth velocity. Explain the pharmacologic basis for this finding in a pediatric rehabilitation context.
back: * Suppression of the HPA axis * Direct inhibition of bone growth at the epiphysis * Interference with growth hormone secretion/action

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Explain the biological mechanism of HPA axis suppression during prolonged corticosteroid use and the rationale for slow drug tapering in a clinical setting.
back: * Exogenous steroids exert negative feedback on CRH and ACTH. * Results in adrenal cortex atrophy. * Abrupt withdrawal causes fatal acute adrenal insufficiency.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: Distinguish between the use of Spironolactone and Eplerenone in managing mineralocorticoid excess during rehabilitation from heart failure.
back: * Spironolactone: Non-selective; causes gynecomastia and menstrual irregularities (anti-androgenic). * Eplerenone: Selective mineralocorticoid antagonist; lacks significant androgen receptor affinity. * Both prevent sodium reabsorption and potassium loss.

category: Discuss the drugs related to rehabilitation
front: State the standard dosing regimen for Hydrocortisone in Addison’s disease to mimic physiological diurnal variation in a rehabilitation setting.
back: * Two-thirds of the dose in the morning * One-third of the dose in the late afternoon * Mimics normal peak early morning cortisol levels

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Folic acid and [___] are administered to patients receiving Pemetrexed chemotherapy to minimize dose-limiting hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicities.
back:
- **Vitamin B12**
- Helps reduce the severity of myelosuppression.
- Decreases the incidence of severe mucositis and diarrhea.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A 12-year-old patient with ALL starting intensive induction chemotherapy is given Allopurinol. Specify the oncology-related complication this agent is intended to prevent.
back:
- **Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS)**
- Prevents **hyperuricemia** by inhibiting xanthine oxidase.
- Avoids crystallization of uric acid in renal tubules.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Describe the molecular role of Dexrazoxane in preventing anthracycline-induced dilated cardiomyopathy.
back:
- **Intracellular iron chelator**.
- Reduces formation of iron-anthracycline complexes.
- Prevents generation of **superoxide free radicals** and subsequent lipid peroxidation of cardiac membranes.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Contrast the pharmacological management of early-onset versus late-onset diarrhea associated with Irinotecan therapy.
back:
- **Early-onset (<24h)**: Cholinergic in nature; treated with **Atropine**.
- **Late-onset (>24h)**: Secretory/inflammatory in nature; treated with high-dose **Loperamide**.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify the hormonal agent often used in oncology for the palliation of cancer-related cachexia due to its ability to stimulate appetite.
back:
- **Megestrol acetate** (a progestin).
- **Corticosteroids** (e.g., Prednisone) also promote weight gain via increased appetite and centripetal fat redistribution.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: To counteract the lethal myelosuppression caused by high-dose Methotrexate, [___] is administered as 'rescue therapy' to bypass the inhibited dihydrofolate reductase.
back:
- **Leucovorin** (Folinic acid).
- Provides a source of **reduced folates** to normal cells.
- Prevents thymineless death in healthy tissues.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: A patient receiving chronic Prednisone as part of a chemotherapy regimen is started on Bisphosphonates. Explain the medical rationale for this drug combination.
back:
- **Prevents glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis**.
- Glucocorticoids suppress intestinal calcium absorption and bone formation.
- Bisphosphonates inhibit the resulting **osteoclast-mediated bone resorption**.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Prednisone induces remission in pediatric patients with Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia (ALL).
back:
- **Lymphocytolytic effect**: Binds cytoplasmic receptors to induce apoptosis in malignant lymphoblasts.
- **Transcription modulation**: Inhibits the synthesis of genes required for lymphocyte proliferation and cytokine release.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Distinguish between the clinical purposes of administering Filgrastim (G-CSF) versus Erythropoietin in a patient with multi-lineage myelosuppression.
back:
- **Filgrastim**: Stimulates neutrophil production to prevent **febrile neutropenia**.
- **Erythropoietin**: Stimulates red blood cell production to treat **chemotherapy-induced anemia**.

category: Describe the drugs used beside surgical resection of various tumours to treat complications
front: Identify the specific hepatic enzyme whose genetic deficiency leads to life-threatening toxicity (severe myelosuppression and diarrhea) upon administration of 5-Fluorouracil.
back:
- **Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD)**.
- DPD is responsible for 80% of 5-FU catabolism.
- Deficiency causes lethal accumulation of active fluorouracil metabolites.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: The glucocorticoid component of the 'R-CHOP' regimen for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, which provides direct lymphocytolytic activity, is [___].
back:
Prednisone.
- Acts as a pro-drug converted to active prednisolone.
- Induces apoptosis in malignant lymphoid cells.
- Essential component for multi-drug synergy.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 10-year-old male with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is started on high-dose Prednisone. Explain the specific cellular mechanism that contributes to the reduction of malignant lymphocyte count.
back:
Lymphocytolysis through apoptosis.
- Glucocorticoids bind intracellular receptors to alter gene transcription.
- Leads to programmed cell death of immature/malignant B and T cells.
- Causes redistribution of cells to lymphoid tissues.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the palliative rationale for including Dexamethasone in an anti-cancer cocktail for a patient suffering from cancer cachexia and cisplatin-induced emesis.
back:
Anti-emetic and orexigenic roles.
- Anti-emetic: Reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.
- Orexigenic: Stimulates appetite to increase caloric intake.
- Mood improvement: Often induces euphoria, improving quality of life.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the primary therapeutic objective of using Prednisone in the 'MOPP' oncology regimen versus its role in managing Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).
back:
Oncology vs. Pulmonary role.
- MOPP: Acts as a direct cytotoxic agent (lymphocytolytic).
- COPD: Used for anti-inflammatory effects and reducing airway edema.
- Both utilize immunosuppressive properties.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the enzymatic inhibition by glucocorticoids that restricts the availability of arachidonic acid, thereby limiting tumor-associated inflammation.
back:
Inhibition of Phospholipase A2.
- Blocks release of arachidonic acid from phospholipids.
- Downregulates cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression.
- Reduces pro-inflammatory prostaglandins and leukotrienes.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the management of hematological malignancies, the glucocorticoid receptors must dimerize and translocate into the [___] to act as transcription factors.
back:
Nucleus.
- Ligand-bound receptors dissociate from heat-shock proteins.
- Dimerized complexes attach to Glucocorticoid Response Elements (GREs).
- Modulates gene expression for pro-apoptotic proteins.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A patient undergoing aggressive chemotherapy for lymphoma develops a puffy face, centripetal fat distribution, and purple striae. Identify the iatrogenic syndrome and its relation to the 'cocktail' component.
back:
Iatrogenic Cushing's Syndrome.
- Caused by high-dose steroid components (e.g., Prednisone).
- Results from chronic glucocorticoid excess.
- Manifests as fat redistribution and protein catabolism.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Distinguish between the use of Dexamethasone and Hydrocortisone in cancer patients regarding mineralocorticoid activity and potency.
back:
Dexamethasone vs. Hydrocortisone.
- Dexamethasone: 25-30x more potent anti-inflammatory; zero salt-retaining activity.
- Hydrocortisone: 1:1 ratio; significant salt retention.
- Dexamethasone is preferred for anti-emetic/edema roles.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the metabolic effects of glucocorticoid therapy on glucose levels in a diabetic patient versus a non-diabetic patient receiving the same cancer treatment.
back:
Exacerbation of Hyperglycemia.
- Glucocorticoids increase gluconeogenesis and decrease glucose uptake.
- Non-diabetic: May develop 'Steroid-induced Diabetes'.
- Diabetic: Requires significant insulin dose adjustment.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the hepatic metabolic conversion required for Prednisone to become pharmacologically active in a patient with Hodgkin lymphoma.
back:
11-beta-hydroxylation.
- Prednisone is an inactive prodrug.
- Converted to Prednisolone in the liver.
- Crucial for patients with impaired hepatic function.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: The standard multi-drug regimen R-CHOP used for treating non-Hodgkin lymphoma includes the glucocorticoid [___].
back:
• Prednisone
• Essential part of the R-CHOP cocktail
• Provides lymphocytolytic action against malignant B-cells

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 45-year-old female receiving paclitaxel for breast cancer is pre-medicated with dexamethasone. State the primary clinical objective of including the glucocorticoid in this protocol.
back:
• Prevention of severe hypersensitivity reactions
• Mitigates taxane-induced dyspnea, urticaria, and hypotension
• Decreases capillary permeability

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the pharmacological mechanism by which dexamethasone functions as an anti-emetic component in various anti-cancer cocktails.
back:
• Likely inhibits prostaglandin synthesis in the brain
• Modifies blood-brain barrier permeability to emetogenic toxins
• Synergizes with 5-HT3 receptor antagonists

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the cytocidal intent of glucocorticoid therapy in hematological malignancies from its role in metastatic solid tumors.
back:
• Hematological: Intended as cytocidal (direct lymphocytolytic effect)
• Solid tumors: Primarily palliative
• Manages peritumor edema, hypercalcemia, and pain

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Describe the physiological role glucocorticoids play in the management of hypercalcemia associated with bone metastases.
back:
• Reduces intestinal calcium absorption
• Suppresses cytokine-mediated bone resorption
• Inhibits osteoclast activity

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Glucocorticoids are administered alongside [___] in advanced prostate cancer to mitigate symptoms of mineralocorticoid excess.
back:
• Abiraterone
• Prevents hypertension and hypokalemia
• Counters mineralocorticoid surge caused by CYP17 inhibition

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: An advanced cancer patient with progressive weight loss and severe anorexia is prescribed a daily glucocorticoid. Identify the specific oncological symptom being targeted by this addition.
back:
• Cancer-associated cachexia and anorexia
• Functions as a pharmacological appetite stimulant
• Enhances caloric intake and general well-being

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Detail the molecular pathway by which the glucocorticoid-receptor complex influences gene expression in a neoplastic cell.
back:
• Binds to cytoplasmic receptors and translocates to the nucleus
• Attaches to Glucocorticoid Response Elements (GREs) on DNA
• Recruits coactivators/corepressors to modulate protein transcription

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Distinguish the effects of glucocorticoids on circulating monocyte/lymphocyte counts versus polymorphonuclear leukocyte counts.
back:
• Monocytes/Lymphocytes: Decreased (redistributed from circulation to lymphoid tissue)
• Neutrophils: Increased (due to increased bone marrow release)
• Hemoglobin/Platelets: Also increased

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the hepatic enzyme family induced by glucocorticoids (e.g., dexamethasone) that may accelerate the clearance of other drugs in an anti-cancer cocktail.
back:
• Cytochrome P450 (specifically CYP3A4)
• Enhances metabolism of co-administered agents
• May necessitate dose adjustments to maintain efficacy

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Prednisone is frequently added to chemotherapy regimens for its ability to increase [___], which helps patients manage cancer-related cachexia and weight loss.
back:
● Appetite
● It stimulates the feeding center to improve nutritional status
● This palliates weight loss associated with advanced malignancy.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 60-year-old male with non-Hodgkin lymphoma receives the R-CHOP protocol. Explain the specific cytotoxic role of the steroid component in this multi-drug cocktail.
back:
● Lymphocytolysis
● Prednisone induces apoptosis in malignant B-lymphocytes
● It redistributes white cells from circulation to lymphoid tissues to reduce tumor burden.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Describe the biological benefit of incorporating high-dose dexamethasone into chemotherapy protocols for patients receiving highly emetogenic drugs like cisplatin.
back:
● Anti-emetic action
● It likely inhibits prostaglandin synthesis and modulates central serotonin signaling
● This reduces the severity of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV).

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the therapeutic intent of Prednisone in the R-CHOP lymphoma protocol with the use of Dexamethasone in the VAD regimen for multiple myeloma.
back:
● R-CHOP: Prednisone acts as a primary cytotoxic/lymphocytolytic agent against B-cells
● VAD: Dexamethasone induces plasma cell apoptosis and can help overcome resistance to other cytotoxic agents.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the specific metabolic complication of malignancy where glucocorticoids are used to antagonize the effects of Vitamin D on intestinal calcium absorption.
back:
● Hypercalcemia of malignancy
● They reduce calcium uptake from the gut
● They are especially effective in steroid-sensitive tumors like lymphomas.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: For Prednisone to exert its active anti-neoplastic effect, it must first undergo 11-β-hydroxylation in the liver to form the active molecule [___].
back:
● Prednisolone
● Prednisone is an inactive prodrug
● This conversion is essential for binding to glucocorticoid receptors in target tissues.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A child undergoing induction therapy for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) with vincristine and prednisone experiences a rapid drop in white cell count. This drug combination facilitates tumor lysis by [___].
back:
● Inducing rapid lymphocytolysis
● Prednisone is highly toxic to immature lymphoblasts
● This releases intracellular contents like purines, requiring monitoring for hyperuricemia.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the molecular step following the binding of a glucocorticoid to its cytoplasmic receptor that allows it to modulate gene expression in cancer cells.
back:
● Dimerization and Nuclear Translocation
● The activated steroid-receptor complex moves into the nucleus
● It binds to Glucocorticoid Response Elements (GREs) to activate or inhibit gene transcription.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Distinguish between the use of Prednisolone and Dexamethasone in oncology based on their mineralocorticoid (salt-retaining) activity.
back:
● Dexamethasone: Zero salt-retaining activity; preferred to avoid fluid retention
● Prednisolone: Has slight mineralocorticoid activity
● Dexamethasone is 30 times more potent than hydrocortisone as an anti-inflammatory.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Glucocorticoids are essential components of curative-intent cocktails for two specific groups of hematologic malignancies known as [___] and [___].
back:
● Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)
● Lymphomas (Hodgkin and Non-Hodgkin)
● They are used for their lymphocytolytic and anti-inflammatory properties.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the management of hematologic malignancies like leukemia and lymphoma, high-dose glucocorticoids are utilized primarily for their [___] effect, which leads to the direct destruction of neoplastic white cells.
back:
• Lymphocytolytic action
• Induces apoptosis in malignant lymphoid cells
• Causes redistribution of lymphocytes from circulation to lymphoid tissue
• May lead to hyperuricemia following rapid cell lysis

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 55-year-old male receiving Cisplatin-based chemotherapy is prescribed high-dose Dexamethasone alongside 5-HT3 antagonists. What is the primary therapeutic rationale for adding this steroid to his anti-cancer cocktail?
back:
• Potent anti-emetic activity
• Reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV)
• Synergizes with other anti-emetics to manage acute and delayed emesis
• Minimizes peritumoral inflammation

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the multi-modal benefit of including Prednisone within the R-CHOP protocol (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Vincristine, Prednisone) for Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma.
back:
• Provides direct cytotoxicity toward malignant B-lymphocytes
• Suppresses inflammatory cytokines and host response to tumor burden
• Acts as a palliative agent by stimulating appetite
• Reduces risk of chemotherapy-induced edema

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A patient with glioblastoma multiforme presents with worsening headaches and focal deficits. Contrast the clinical goal of using Dexamethasone in this CNS malignancy versus its role in a systemic lymphoproliferative disorder.
back:
• CNS: Specifically reduces vasogenic peritumoral edema and intracranial pressure
• Systemic: Acts as a primary lymphocytolytic cytotoxic agent
• Dexamethasone is preferred for CNS due to high potency and zero salt-retention

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify two high-yield, non-cytotoxic palliative reasons for including Prednisone in drug cocktails for terminal patients with advanced metastatic disease.
back:
• Appetite stimulation (combating cancer-related cachexia)
• Improvement of mood and overall sense of well-being (euphoria)
• Reduction of pain caused by inflammatory pressure around tumor sites
• Potentiation of anti-emetic nutritional intake

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In various anti-cancer cocktails, the specific synthetic glucocorticoid often added primarily to counteract neoplastic cachexia and stimulate appetite is [___].
back:
• Prednisone
• Stimulates intermediary metabolism
• Increases plasma glucose levels
• Promotes weight gain and well-being

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 55-year-old male receiving highly emetogenic chemotherapy for a solid tumor is prescribed Dexamethasone as part of his pre-treatment cocktail. What is the physiological purpose of this addition?
back:
• Antiemetic action
• Reduces prostaglandins in the CNS
• Synergizes with 5-HT3 antagonists
• Prevents chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV)

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the lymphocytolytic mechanism by which glucocorticoids directly treat hematologic malignancies like Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).
back:
• Bind to cytoplasmic receptors (hGRα)
• Translocate to nucleus and modify transcription
• Induce apoptosis in lymphoid cells
• Redistribute lymphocytes to lymphoid tissues

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the utility of Prednisolone in the R-CHOP regimen for Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma with its role in managing hypercalcemia of malignancy.
back:
• R-CHOP: Acts as a direct cytotoxic agent
• Hypercalcemia: Antagonizes Vitamin D effects
• Reduces intestinal calcium absorption
• Decreases bone resorption in lymphoid tumors

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Describe the clinical rationale for including high-dose Dexamethasone in cocktails for patients with primary CNS malignancies or metastatic brain tumors.
back:
• Manages peritumoral edema
• Decreases capillary permeability
• Stabilizes the blood-brain barrier
• Relieves increased intracranial pressure

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the standard curative regimen for pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), glucocorticoids are essential components typically paired with [___] and Vincristine.
back:
• Asparaginase (L-asparaginase)
• Cocktail induces remission in >90% of children
• Targets asparagine-dependent neoplastic cells
• Synergistic lymphocytolytic induction

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 60-year-old patient with Multiple Myeloma is treated with the VAD protocol (Vincristine, Doxorubicin, and Dexamethasone). Analyze why Dexamethasone is specifically selected over Hydrocortisone in this cocktail.
back:
• Higher anti-inflammatory potency
• Minimal mineralocorticoid activity
• Reduced risk of salt and water retention
• Superior synergy in lymphoid cell lysis

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain how glucocorticoids modulate the B-cell activation pathway to contribute to the success of the R-CHOP regimen in Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma.
back:
• Inhibits NF-κB transcription factor
• Decreases proinflammatory cytokine production
• Blocks mitotic spindle formation in synergy with Vincristine
• Triggers programmed cell death in malignant B-cells

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the anti-inflammatory metabolic loop versus the intermediaries metabolism loop utilized by steroids in palliative cancer care.
back:
• Anti-inflammatory: Inhibits Phospholipase A2 and prostaglandins
• Intermediary: Favors gluconeogenesis and lipolysis
• Combined effect: Reduced pain and increased energy
• Supports tolerance of aggressive chemotherapy

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the primary biochemical fact that distinguishes the use of Prednisone as a 'pro-drug' within oncological cocktails.
back:
• Requires 11-β-hydroxylation in the liver
• Converted to active Prednisolone
• Effectiveness dependent on hepatic function
• Standard component of CMF and R-CHOP

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the management of childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), Prednisone is standardly administered in combination with the microtubule inhibitor [___] for remission induction.
back:
Vincristine (Oncovin).
- This combination, often with Asparaginase, is the cornerstone for inducing remission in pediatric lymphoid malignancies.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A patient with lymphocytic leukemia shows a sharp decline in peripheral white cell count shortly after starting high-dose Dexamethasone. Explain the pathophysiology of this response.
back:
- Redistribution of circulating lymphocytes to lymphoid tissues.
- Direct induction of apoptosis (lymphocytolysis) in neoplastic cells.
- Inhibition of DNA synthesis in the S-phase of the cell cycle.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Beyond direct cytotoxicity, identify two supportive care benefits of including Dexamethasone in high-dose Cisplatin or Doxorubicin cocktails.
back:
- Potent anti-emetic effect (reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting).
- Appetite stimulation (improves nutritional status in cachectic cancer patients).

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the primary therapeutic objective of including Prednisone in the R-CHOP regimen for lymphoma versus using Dexamethasone in a patient with a primary glioblastoma.
back:
- R-CHOP: Prednisone acts as a cytotoxic/lympholytic agent to kill malignant B-cells.
- Glioblastoma: Dexamethasone is primarily used as an anti-inflammatory to reduce peritumoral edema and intracranial pressure.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
