front: Describe the essential pharmacological step required when concluding a 6-month high-dose steroid course in a patient with multiple myeloma.
back:
Gradual dose tapering.
- Prevents acute adrenal insufficiency (Adrenal Crisis).
- Allows the HPA axis, suppressed by long-term feedback inhibition, to recover natural cortisol production.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the highly effective R-CHOP regimen utilized for aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphomas, the component 'P' stands for the synthetic glucocorticoid [___].
back:
Prednisone.
- It is often interchanged with Prednisolone depending on hepatic function, as Prednisone is a prodrug.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 60-year-old male with Multiple Myeloma presents with severe lethargy and a serum calcium of 14 mg/dL. Explain how the addition of Glucocorticoids to his regimen addresses this complication.
back:
- Antagonizes the effects of Vitamin D on intestinal calcium absorption.
- Reduces bone resorption by inhibiting the growth of malignant, cytokine-producing plasma cells.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Detail the molecular sequence that occurs after a glucocorticoid molecule enters a neoplastic lymphoid cell and binds its cytoplasmic receptor.
back:
- Receptor dimerization and translocation to the nucleus.
- Binding to Glucocorticoid Response Elements (GREs) on DNA.
- Altered transcription of genes, leading to increased pro-apoptotic proteins and decreased pro-survival signals.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the metabolic effect of glucocorticoid therapy on the liver versus peripheral skeletal muscle in a patient undergoing chemotherapy.
back:
- Liver: Stimulates gluconeogenesis and glycogen synthesis (hyperglycemic effect).
- Muscle: Stimulates protein catabolism (muscle wasting) to provide amino acid substrates for liver gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the specific phase of the cell cycle where glucocorticoids are most active in inhibiting the proliferation of malignant lymphoid cells.
back:
The G1 phase.
- They inhibit the transition from G1 to the S-phase, often leading to cell cycle arrest and subsequent apoptosis.

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the R-CHOP chemotherapy cocktail used for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, the drug [___] provides the essential steroid component for induction of lymphocytolysis.
back:
- Prednisone (or Prednisolone)
- Induces apoptosis in malignant B-cells
- Integral part of many lymphoid malignancy regimens

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 55-year-old patient with lung cancer experiences severe nausea during cisplatin infusion despite ondansetron therapy. What specific glucocorticoid is added to the anti-cancer cocktail to manage chemotherapy-induced vomiting?
back:
- Dexamethasone
- Acts on the emetic center
- Potentiates 5-HT3 antagonists and NK1 inhibitors

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the primary cellular mechanism by which glucocorticoids like Prednisone exert their anti-neoplastic effect in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).
back:
- Binds to intracellular cytoplasmic receptors
- Modulates gene transcription
- Induces programmed cell death (apoptosis) in lymphoid lineages

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the therapeutic rationale for preferring Dexamethasone over Prednisone in patients requiring glucocorticoid-based cocktails for intracranial malignancies.
back:
- Higher anti-inflammatory potency
- Superior blood-brain barrier penetration
- Zero mineralocorticoid activity (reduces risk of worsening edema)
- Longer biological half-life

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the pharmacological rationale for combining Prednisone with Abiraterone in the management of metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer.
back:
- Compensates for Abiraterone-induced cortisol reduction
- Suppresses ACTH drive
- Prevents secondary mineralocorticoid excess (hypertension/hypokalemia)

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In palliative anti-cancer cocktails, the glucocorticoid Prednisone is often included to specifically manage the metabolic and nutritional complication of [___].
back:
- Cancer-associated anorexia or cachexia
- Stimulates appetite
- Enhances sense of well-being (euphoric effect)

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A 60-year-old patient on the VAD regimen for refractory myeloma has been on high-dose dexamethasone for several months. Why must the clinician implement a gradual tapering schedule rather than abrupt cessation?
back:
- To prevent acute adrenal insufficiency
- To allow the suppressed HPA axis to recover
- To avoid withdrawal syndrome (lethargy, arthralgia)

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Describe the synergistic biochemical mechanism of glucocorticoids when combined with Immunomodulatory Drugs (IMiDs) like Lenalidomide in Multiple Myeloma cocktails.
back:
- Downregulates IL-6 (a vital growth factor)
- Enhances T-cell and NK-cell mediated cytotoxicity
- Potentiates apoptosis via caspase activation

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the biological half-lives of Prednisone and Dexamethasone as it relates to their dosing frequency in chemotherapeutic schedules.
back:
- Prednisone: Intermediate-acting (12–36 hours)
- Dexamethasone: Long-acting (36–55 hours)
- Dexamethasone allows for less frequent pulse-dosing

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the primary metabolic side effect that requires mandatory blood glucose monitoring when high-dose corticosteroids are included in anti-cancer cocktails.
back:
- Hyperglycemia
- Can lead to steroid-induced Diabetes Mellitus
- Result of increased gluconeogenesis and peripheral insulin resistance

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In multi-drug regimens for acute lymphoblastic leukemia and lymphomas, the primary cytotoxic mechanism of glucocorticoids is identified as [___].
back:
● Lymphocytolysis
● Causes redistribution of lymphocytes from blood to lymphoid tissues
● Triggers apoptosis in malignant lymphoid cells
● Essential for debulking lymphoid tumor burden

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A patient with advanced lung cancer develops severe cachexia and weight loss. Beyond its anti-inflammatory effects, identify the non-cytotoxic rationale for adding Prednisone to this patient's cocktail.
back:
● Appetite stimulation
● Counteracts cancer-associated wasting (cachexia)
● Increases caloric intake and promotes weight gain
● Enhances overall sense of well-being (euphoria)

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Explain the role of high-dose Dexamethasone as a supportive component in highly emetogenic chemotherapy cocktails.
back:
● Anti-emetic activity
● Reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV)
● Potentiates other anti-emetics like 5-HT3 antagonists
● Often utilized in regimens containing cisplatin

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: In the R-CHOP regimen for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, contrast the molecular target of Prednisone with that of Cyclophosphamide.
back:
● Prednisone: Targets intracellular glucocorticoid receptors (induces lymphocytolysis)
● Cyclophosphamide: Targets DNA directly (forms covalent cross-links)
● Prednisone focuses on immune cell redistribution
● Cyclophosphamide focuses on DNA replication blockade

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Identify the primary clinical objective of administering glucocorticoids to patients with metastatic solid tumors experiencing increased intracranial pressure.
back:
● Reduction of peritumoral edema
● Decreases capillary permeability in the tumor microenvironment
● Lowers intracranial pressure and inflammatory swelling
● Improves neurological symptoms during palliative care

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Prednisone is frequently utilized in oral anti-cancer cocktails; however, it must first be activated in the liver into [___] to be biologically functional.
back:
● Prednisolone
● Requires 11-beta-hydroxylation to become active
● Liver microsomal enzymes perform this conversion
● Active form then binds to cytoplasmic steroid receptors

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: A patient with multiple myeloma presents with lethargy, polyuria, and a serum calcium of 14 mg/dL. Explain why glucocorticoids are included in the emergency management.
back:
● Management of Hypercalcemia of Malignancy
● Inhibits bone resorption and antagonizes Vitamin D
● Decreases intestinal calcium absorption
● Directly cytolytic to malignant plasma cells

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Describe how glucocorticoids modulate the inflammatory microenvironment in solid tumors to prevent treatment-related damage.
back:
● Inhibition of proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1, TNF-alpha)
● Blocks Phospholipase A2 to reduce prostaglandin synthesis
● Stabilizes mast cell and basophil membranes
● Reduces capillary permeability and localized swelling

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Contrast the cytotoxic versus the 'permissive' role of glucocorticoids when used in varied anti-cancer therapy combinations.
back:
● Cytotoxic: Direct lymphocytolysis in hematological cancers
● Permissive: Restores vascular/bronchial responsiveness to catecholamines
● Cytotoxic role debulks tumor cell count
● Permissive role maintains homeostasis during stress

category: Explain the role of glucocorticoids as part of various anti-cancer cocktails
front: Name the physiological phenomenon by which glucocorticoids lower circulating monocyte and eosinophil levels during cancer treatment.
back:
● Redistribution
● Shifts cells from circulation to lymphoid tissue
● Not primarily caused by immediate systemic destruction
● Results in transiently lowered peripheral blood counts

category: g
front: In the most common form of Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH), a deficiency in the enzyme [___] leads to reduced cortisol synthesis and compensatory ACTH elevation.
back:
21-alpha hydroxylase (P450c21).
• Leads to accumulation of 17-hydroxyprogesterone.
• Diverts precursors to the adrenal androgen pathway.
• Clinically causes virilization in females.

category: g
front: A patient being treated for Hodgkin lymphoma develops a dry cough and exertional dyspnea. Imaging reveals pulmonary fibrosis. Which cell-cycle specific antibiotic is most likely responsible?
back:
Bleomycin.
• Acts by generating free radicals that cause DNA strand scission.
• Low levels of inactivating hydrolase in the lung.
• Causes 'Bleomycin lung' (irreversible pulmonary fibrosis).

category: g
front: Describe the genomic mechanism of action utilized by corticosteroids once they diffuse into a target cell's cytoplasm.
back:
• Bind to cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptors.
• Receptor-hormone complex dimerizes and translocates into the nucleus.
• Binds to Glucocorticoid Response Elements (GREs) on DNA.
• Upregulates or downregulates transcription of target genes.

category: g
front: Contrast the primary dose-limiting toxicities of the M-phase specific Vinca alkaloids: Vincristine and Vinblastine.
back:
• Vincristine: Dose-limiting neurotoxicity (peripheral neuropathy, foot drop, constipation).
• Vinblastine: Dose-limiting myelosuppression (bone marrow suppression).
• Both inhibit tubulin polymerization to prevent spindle formation.

category: g
front: State the pharmacological mechanism by which Ketoconazole acts as an inhibitor in the treatment of Cushing syndrome.
back:
• Nonselective inhibitor of steroid hormone synthesis.
• Blocks multiple cytochrome P450 enzymes (P450c11, P450c17).
• Inhibits cholesterol side-chain cleavage.
• Effectively reduces both adrenal and gonadal steroid production.

category: g
front: To prevent hemorrhagic cystitis caused by the toxic metabolite acrolein, [___] is administered to neutralize cyclophosphamide products in the bladder.
back:
Mesna (Sodium 2-mercaptoethane sulfonate).
• Reacts chemically with acrolein in the urine.
• Mandatory for high-dose cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide therapy.
• Always used alongside aggressive hydration.

category: g
front: A male patient with heart failure develops painful gynecomastia while taking Spironolactone. Which alternative aldosterone antagonist should be prescribed to avoid this side effect?
back:
Eplerenone.
• Highly selective for the mineralocorticoid receptor.
• Lacks the affinity for androgen/progesterone receptors seen in spironolactone.
• Prevents gynecomastia and menstrual irregularities.

category: g
front: Explain how Leucovorin (Folinic Acid) acts as a 'rescue' agent during high-dose Methotrexate therapy.
back:
• Methotrexate inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Leucovorin provides a reduced folate source (N5-formyl-THF).
• Bypasses the blocked DHFR enzyme to replenish folate pools.
• Protects normal cells from lethal thymineless death.

category: g
front: Contrast Primary vs. Secondary Adrenocortical Insufficiency regarding mineralocorticoid (Aldosterone) levels.
back:
• Primary (Addison's): Cortex destroyed; lack of both cortisol and aldosterone.
• Secondary (Pituitary): Lack of ACTH; mineralocorticoids preserved.
• Aldosterone remains intact in secondary cases due to Renin-Angiotensin regulation.

category: g
front: Specify the molecular mechanism responsible for the irreversible cardiotoxicity associated with Anthracyclines like Doxorubicin.
back:
• Generation of iron-dependent oxygen free radicals.
• Causes membrane lipid peroxidation and DNA scission.
• Results in dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy.
• Dexrazoxane (iron chelator) can be used for protection.
